**Overview**
Hey this is Rohit (CEO/co-founder) writing this. I find most JDs to be quite impersonal and bland. We do things a bit differently here at String. So to start off, I appreciate you for taking the time to read this and for considering us.
  
  
**We’re building the most comprehensive platform to collect and structure data from the web.**
**Customers ranging from the world’s largest hedge funds**
to seed-stage startups use String to pull 30M+ rows of structured web data per week (that’s literally 50+ rows every second).
  
  
**We’re generating 7 figures in ARR and are growing double digit % MoM.**
We have found initial PMF and are now building our delivery team to accelerate growth. We’ve done everything so far with a lean team of < 10 people and we recently raised a seed round (unannounced) from leading VCs and angels in our space (Auren Hoffman, Charlie Songhurst, and many more).
  
  
**We’re working with the best.**
We are known in our niche of finance as the best product and therefore are working with most of the largest hedge funds, PE, and VC firms. You will get the opportunity to work directly with decision makers at these firms and help them win.
  
  
**We are looking for the right person to join us as our founding FDE**
on this exciting journey! If you want to help build our FDE function from the ground up and operate well in unstructured environments, we would love to meet you!
  
  
What do we do
  
  
Today any business that wants to collect web data has to jump through many hoops:
  
  

* Build infrastructure to send thousands of requests to websites
* Build technology to avoid getting detected as a bot (very hard to do at scale)
* Code individual scripts for every website they want to scrape
* Fix all those scripts as websites change, and
* Ensure consistent data quality across runs

We solve all of these problems for them so that they never have to worry about scraping. Thus, we 1) significantly improve their end products driving millions in revenue and 2) save them hundreds of thousands of dollars in engineering costs.
  
  
Our end customers use our product to
  
  

* Make better decisions. E.g. how much is Lululemon discounting their products and should I therefore buy their stock.
* Fundamentally support their core products. E.g. I’m an AI legal tech company and need to scrape tons of laws across state & local government websites.

Building this would have been impossible before the AI revolution. We have a unique opportunity to build the first platform where anyone can collect structured data across any website with just a prompt. And we’re excited to be at the forefront of solving this problem for our customers.
  
  
What will you do
  
  

* Work directly with our largest customers to solve their scraping problems
* Own customer requests end to end to ensure they’re beyond happy

+ This is the energy we’re looking for: ‘What do you want? Cool, we'll build it.’ Come back the next day and say, ‘Did this fix your problem? What else do you want?’

* Help define the product roadmap for our broader engineering team - you’re at the frontlines and have the most context into what customers are requesting
* Manage our scraping engineers who will report directly to you - they help build & maintain scraper pipelines for our customers.

Who are we looking for
  
  

* 3+ years of engineering experience
* 1+ years of experience directly working with customers in some capacity (solutions engineering, technical account manager, sales engineer etc)
* High raw intellectual horsepower and creative problem solving
* Proven success in improving NPS and/or sales velocity of an organization
* Based in or willing to move to NYC

**Nice To Haves**

* Experience at a early/growth stage startup
* Has worked with our ICPs or buyer profiles before (head of data, investment analyst, founder)

Why join us
  
  
It’s not often that a startup is hiring their first FDE after hitting 7 figures in ARR and in initial stages of PMF. The list of companies is a handful when you filter for NYC, which we believe is the best city to live in! For the right person, this will be an opportunity for immense career growth both to own responsibility beyond the typical engineering role and to move into managing other engineers much faster than otherwise possible.
  
  
This role will transform your career and give you the badge to go on to whatever you want to do next. We believe you’ll have the skills to be a 10x asset to any startup you join in the future - the type of person that hot startups want as an early executive. Or to start your own company.
  
  
We’re in a unique time in history where AI is giving engineers unprecedented leverage. However, our customers can’t leverage this for scraping because they still get blocked by antibot, they don’t have the infra to scale scrapes, they haven’t built data quality validation etc. We’ve solved all of these core challenges and now need to best help them wherever they are in their scraping journey. You’ll be at the frontlines of helping the biggest financial and tech institutions solve these pain points.
  
  
Interview process
  
  

* Initial conversation with Rohit (30 mins)
* Code challenge with engineer (45 mins)
* Systems design interview with Logan (45 mins)
* Culture interview with founders (1 hour, ideally in person)

Values & team
  
  
Feel free to read through our team values to see if working with us will be a good fit for you. If you get excited from reading the values page, it’s likely a good fit and vice versa.
  
  
**Logan (CTO):**
Leading engineering and has extensive web scraping & AI experience. Ships like a 10 person engineering team (Rohit bragging for him). Previously worked as the founding engineer at Nourish (YC W21, now unicorn) and as a software engineer at C3 AI. Has arbitraged Polymarket, frontran ICOs & Coinbase listings, and wrote a chess engine. TLDR has spedrun the full tech bro starter pack.
  
  
**Rohit (CEO):**
Leading GTM and has signed dozens of enterprise deals including 6 of the 10 largest hedge funds while spending half his time coding. Previously worked as a consultant at Bain and cofounded two startups in college, one of them with Logan called CampusOven.
  
  
**Engineers:**
We have 7 more great engineers on the team who help build and maintain the full end to end product. We’re lucky to have such passionate and thoughtful engineers on the team.
  
  
**Sales:**
We recently onboarded 2 great AEs to help accelerate growth.
  
  
**Compensation & Benefits**
We’re building an exceptional team and so want to be generous on compensation. Our philosophy is that base compensation is for living expenses and equity is for upside. We want you to be able to give your all and benefit proportionately from your contributions, without worrying about living expenses.
  
  
So our compensation structure is a base salary competitive with other seed stage startups and generous equity relative to other startups. We know that part of the excitement of joining a startup is the upside and to feel like an owner - that’s why we left our corporate jobs.
  
  
**More Concrete Information**

* 140k-160k base, 0.1%-0.5% equity (US based only)
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Beautiful office in Midtown
* Meals comped at office and tons of snacks
* Annual international offsite (and additional travel)
* Flexible PTO

Locations: New York (hybrid)

Job Description

New AI models and coding tools ship every few weeks, and our engineers put them on real projects as soon as they land. What we learn shapes how our team works and what we recommend to the companies we partner with.

This role starts on our AI Development Experience projects. You'll work next to engineers who have shipped production software for years. They'll hand you hard problems and help you through them.

What the work looks like

To begin with, you'll build and improve the tools and workflows our engineers use to ship with AI. That could be an internal agent, coding guidelines that people actually follow, or a way to tell when a new model makes our output worse. The stack is mostly TypeScript and Node.js, with React on the front end.

Over time you'll also work with clients, so we're hiring someone who's comfortable in a meeting and can explain their work clearly to engineers and non-engineers alike.

AI coding tools are part of the job, and you'll use them every day. You own every line you ship, including the ones you didn't type.

What we're looking for

* You build things without being asked. A side project, or a script that fixed something annoying at your last job. We'll ask you about them.
* You get unstuck. When something is unclear, you ask, or you make a reasonable call and write down what you assumed. You raise blockers the same day.
* You use AI tools with judgment. You've worked with Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot and you've seen them get things wrong. You read the difference before you commit it.
* You think about the next person in the codebase. You reuse what's already there and flag anything that looks insecure, even when it's outside your ticket.
* You're comfortable with change. AI tooling moves fast, and a project you start may change direction within a week. Some people find that energizing. If you'd rather work to a predictable roadmap, this probably isn't the right fit.
* You can come from anywhere. A CS degree, a bootcamp, internships or teaching yourself all work. In the interview we look at what you've built and how you reason through a problem.

How we interview

There are two conversations and no algorithm puzzles.

This role applies engineering judgment across a broad and evolving set of activities, including platform configuration, integrations, governed data access, retrieval pipelines, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. The AI Engineer works closely with Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Data, Operations, and business stakeholders to translate emerging AI capabilities into secure and compliant business outcomes.

* Hands-on experience designing enterprise AI solutions, including prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool calling, context engineering, evaluation frameworks, agentic workflows, and production AI application delivery

* Understanding of HIPAA and the importance of patient data privacy

**About Tutor**
We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.
  
  
Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
  
  
Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.
  
  
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
  
  
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
  
  
**The Role**
As our first Applied AI Engineer on Finance, you'll build the operating system for how Tutor runs its finances: planning and forecasting, billing, the close, and the numbers leadership and the board run the company on. You'll design the process flows and change the shape of the work, and you'll do it by writing a lot of software: building whole workflows, tools, and AI agents from scratch rather than living in spreadsheets.
  
  
This is a technical role where you write and own software, and you'll embed as a true member of our finance team, owning outcomes for that team through technology. You'll have full visibility into what finance does across the business, and you'll treat finance as part of the wider Tutor system: our robots, deployments, customers, and data. Tutor sells robot labor with usage-based pricing, so billing, revenue, and unit economics all depend on what the robots actually do.
  
  
You'll join our forward-deployed AI engineering team: a strategic team of engineers already embedded across deployment, manufacturing, maintenance, and hardware and software engineering, using AI to change how each of those functions works. You'll be its first engineer dedicated to finance.
  
  
You'll start by taking over and extending finance tools we've already built. From there you'll steward the area as the business grows, using the tools alongside the team and improving them to handle more scale and complexity.
  
  
**What you'll work on**

* Architect and build the systems finance runs on, including FP&A and forecasting tools integrated with our existing systems, with live dashboards and analytics in place of spreadsheets
* Automate the close with software and AI agents: reconciliations, AP/AR, spend review, and variance explanations
* Own the usage-to-invoice pipeline, so billing reconciles to what our robots actually did
* Build the financial data layer that joins accounting, spend, CRM, billing, and robot operations data
* Model the business in code: pricing and deal economics, fleet and financing scenarios, and the annual operating plan
* Take over and extend the tools we already have, and keep them working as the team and the business scale
* Build in the controls, checks, and audit trails that let the numbers hold up to auditors, lenders, and investors

**What we're looking for**

* You've architected and shipped a real system end to end, whether product, internal tooling, data, or infrastructure, and can explain the design choices behind it
* You write working software (Python, SQL, APIs, data pipelines) and build with LLMs and AI coding tools every day
* A technical background with a spike somewhere else: finance, economics, operations, strategy, or founding something. Your path probably hasn't been linear
* Demonstrated passion for, interest in, or experience with finance, and a fundamental understanding of how a company's finances work. You don't need to have held a finance title
* Precision: you build checks, sweat edge cases, and hate a number you can't explain
* High slope: you learn fast, take on ambiguous problems with little direction, and want to make a mark
* You want to be embedded in a business function. This is not a product engineering or research role

**Nice to haves**

* Usage-based or subscription billing systems
* A modern accounting and spend stack, and BI tools
* Technical program management (especially FinOps or fintech), product management, or a past founder or first-of-function role
* Hardware unit economics, equipment financing, or other capital-intensive businesses

**Why Tutor?**
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
  
  
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
  
  
**Benefits**
We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:
  
  

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

We are seeking a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to lead the design and delivery of the platform’s AI capabilities. This is an opportunity to take ownership of systems that move beyond experimentation into production. Qualified candidates will bring at least five years of applied machine learning experience, including hands-on work with embeddings, retrieval systems, and prompt engineering. Experience with fine-tuning language models, structured JSON generation, and human-feedback approaches such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is important. Familiarity with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, distillation, or other techniques for improving model behavior.

**Summary**
About the Product
  
  
Concierge is Guidewire's omnichannel AI agent for P&C carriers. It answers the phone when a policyholder has just had an accident, takes first notice of loss, asks the questions a good adjuster would ask, and writes a clean claim into ClaimCenter. It runs in production today with real carriers and real policyholders, not as a demo.
  
  
Two things make this harder than a typical chatbot. First, it has synchronous voice: latency is a product requirement, not a metric on a dashboard. Second, FNOL is a regulated event where the quality of the intake determines the eventual cost of the claim. A missed question early is a bigger loss reserve later.
  
  
**The Role**
You will build, evaluate, and harden the agent itself: the orchestration, the context it sees, the tools it can call, and the evals that tell us whether a change made it better or just different.
  
  
Our rollout philosophy is a dimmer, not a light switch. We widen the agent's autonomy one notch at a time, and every notch has to be earned with evidence. Much of your work is producing that evidence, then acting on what it says.
  
  
**Job Description**
**What you'll do**

* Own end-to-end slices of the agent: prompt and context architecture, retrieval over policy and coverage data, tool and API calls into core claims systems, and handoff to a human when the agent should stop.
* Build and run the eval loop, golden sets, trajectory evaluation, LLM-as-judge, error analysis on real production call traces, and make it the thing that gates releases.
* Drive containment and resolution rates up without trading away accuracy, and instrument the system well enough that we can tell which of the two moved.
* Work directly on the voice path: turn-taking, interruption, latency budgets, and the telephony layer underneath (LiveKit, SIP).
* Sit in on carrier calls and listen to recordings. The best fixes usually come from hearing where the conversation went sideways, not from reading the logs.

**What We're Looking For**

* Building and deploying AI applications. You've shipped an LLM application that real users depend on, and you know that the hard part is that the output is not predictable. You're fluent in the building blocks LLMs, context engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, and you have real ML and deep learning depth underneath that fluency. Most importantly, you know how to make an unpredictable system behave predictably enough to trust: disciplined evals, error analysis, and statistical measurement rather than vibes and a handful of spot checks.
* Software engineering fundamentals. You can reason about cost, latency, reliability, and scalability as tradeoffs rather than goals, and you know which ones you're making. You've designed data stores and distributed systems, you write tests, and you take security and privacy seriously while advocating CI/CD process automation. We handle claims data, recorded calls, and PII under carrier and regulatory scrutiny.
* Using coding agents. You work with coding agents daily and you're good at it: managing their context, deciding when a spec is worth writing and when it isn't, giving them verifiers so they can close their own loops, and knowing when to intervene versus leave them alone. You also keep changing how you work as the tooling changes, rather than settling into a 2025 workflow.
* Shaping the build. You won't be handed a finished spec. You'll be in the room where we decide what the agent should do next, which means you need product sense and enough insurance context to argue about it. You'll know when to put an MVP in front of a carrier next week and when a claims workflow demands that we slow down and get it right the first time.

Underneath all four: you keep learning. This field looks different every six months and we expect to keep changing our minds.
  
  
**Nice to have**

* Real-time or streaming voice systems (ASR, TTS, telephony, SBC/SIPREC)
* Insurance, claims, or another regulated domain where being wrong has a cost attached
* Experience building internal eval or observability tooling other engineers actually adopted.
* Experience in Machine learning principles, or have experience in model experimentations, training and deploying models in Productions.
* Experience in P&C Insurance or exposure to Guidewire products and services.
* Prompt or pipeline optimization frameworks (DSPy, GEPA) applied to a production system

**How To Apply**
Send a short note about something you shipped where the model's unpredictability was the central problem, and what you did about it. We care more about that than about a list of frameworks.

**About the Team**
The Autonomous Vehicle Microcontrollers team develops embedded platform software that provides the foundation for AV systems. Our software communicates with sensors, supports vehicle operation, provides observability, manages system health, and enables reliable operation of vehicle and platform functions.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Software Engineer on the AV MCU Platform team, you will independently own moderate-scope software features, components, or sub-projects related to MCU01. You will contribute across the development lifecycle‚ from requirements and design through implementation, integration, testing, debugging, documentation, and release support. You will work closely with systems, hardware, safety, cybersecurity, integration, and validation teams to deliver production-quality embedded software.
  
  
Come build the future of self-driving at GM.
  
  
**What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)**

* Reproduce and diagnose software failures using logs, traces, debugger data, telemetry, test evidence, and controlled experiments.
* Perform structured root-cause analysis for crashes, memory faults, timing issues, race conditions, communication failures, watchdog resets, and unexpected state transitions as applicable.
* Design, develop, integrate, and maintain embedded C software for multi-core microcontrollers.
* Implement moderate-scope features, enhancements, integrations, and defect fixes within the assigned software component or subsystem.
* Develop across the applicable automotive embedded software stack, including BSP, BSW, middleware, RTOS services, drivers, and application software.
* Write maintainable, modular, efficient, and testable code consistent with team coding standards.
* Implement robust handling for initialization, state transitions, communication errors, diagnostics, degraded operation, watchdog events, and fault recovery as applicable.
* Analyze the impact of software changes on interfaces, timing, memory, CPU utilization, configuration, and dependent components.

**Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)**

* Bachelors degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related STEM field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Ability to diagnose software issues using logs, traces, debuggers, test results, and other technical evidence.
* 2+ years of experience building and shipping production quality embedded software
* Background in C Embedded Software development
* Understanding software development lifecycle practices, source control, code reviews, continuous integration, and issue tracking.
* Experience working with RTOS (such as QNX, FreeRTOS, OSEK, etc.)
* Good communication skills, capable of switching between high-level and detailed discussions

**Preferred Qualifications (Nice-to-Have)**

* Experience with robotics, autonomous vehicles, automotive embedded systems, or ADAS development
* Experience working with AUTOSAR
* Experience working in a Safety Critical Embedded Software Environment (ISO 26262, DO-178C, MIL-STD-882E)
* Experience with JIRA, DOORs NG, Confluence, Github, Lauterbach, Visual Studio Code.
* Experience developing software that scales to millions of instances and managing it
* Ability to adapt and operate under ambiguity, going from quick code prototypes to long-term plans on brief time horizons
* 2+ years of experience building and shipping production quality embedded software
* Masters degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related STEM field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

Machine Learning Engineer / Predictive Analytics Consultant
  
  
Preferred locations: Birmingham, Alabama, or Dallas, Texas
  
  
**About The Company**
Vaco LLC connects organizations with skilled professionals to address evolving business and technology needs. This opportunity supports an established machine learning team at an organization with a mature cloud and big data environment. The team is expanding its delivery capacity and advancing the use of predictive analytics across the business. Its focus is on moving beyond traditional dashboards and reporting toward forecasting and forward-looking solutions that help teams make informed decisions.
  
  
**About The Role**
Vaco LLC is seeking a hands-on Machine Learning Engineer / Predictive Analytics Consultant to help build and scale practical, enterprise-ready analytics solutions. In this role, you will work primarily on sales and marketing forecasting, predictive modeling, and business intelligence transformation initiatives. You will partner with stakeholders to understand business needs, shape ambiguous requests into clear analytical approaches, and deliver models that support measurable business outcomes.
  
  
This is a collaborative yet autonomous position for an experienced practitioner who can work with minimal direction, manage evolving priorities, and solve complex problems independently. You will join a growing team with an active pipeline of analytics work and contribute to faster project delivery and broader predictive analytics capabilities. The preferred work locations are Birmingham, Alabama, and Dallas, Texas.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Candidates should have at least five years of experience in machine learning, predictive analytics, data science, or a related data-focused field. Strong hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL is required. Experience with Spark or PySpark and Snowflake is beneficial. You should have experience developing machine learning and predictive models from the ground up, working with large-scale datasets, and using distributed data processing environments.
  
  
A strong understanding of statistical analysis, forecasting, predictive modeling, and machine learning methodologies is essential. Experience in a cloud-based analytics ecosystem such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud is expected. The successful candidate will demonstrate analytical thinking, sound problem-solving skills, independent judgment, and the ability to translate business challenges into scalable technical solutions. Preferred experience includes sales or marketing analytics, business performance forecasting, enterprise machine learning, Databricks or similar platforms, and direct communication with business stakeholders or leadership teams.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Design, develop, test, validate, and deploy machine learning and predictive analytics models using large structured and unstructured datasets. Create forecasting solutions for sales, marketing, and operational initiatives, selecting appropriate methods and optimizing models for reliable performance. Conduct exploratory data analysis, engineer features, compare modeling approaches, tune parameters, and evaluate results.
  
  
Collaborate with business partners to clarify objectives, define analytical requirements, and turn ambiguous requests into actionable data solutions. Use the organization’s cloud and big data environment to support scalable analytics delivery. Help address a growing backlog by improving project throughput and accelerating delivery timelines. Work across analytics, engineering, and business teams, communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to stronger, more efficient predictive analytics processes.

onepot is automating chemistry. Our goal is to enable a self-improvement loop for chemistry by combining AI and advanced robotics. In this loop, AI systems design experiments, robotic systems execute them, and the resulting data improves the next generation of models.

This goal can only be achieved by bringing together people from different backgrounds: ML engineers, chemists, computer scientists, and hardware engineers. We are building a small, unusually ambitious team and are looking for a machine learning researcher to join us to help train the next generation of chemistry models.

We train models for a wide range of tasks, including reaction planning and outcome, input material costs, and mass spectra prediction. Most of these models are state-of-the-art; many are trained on proprietary datasets that are larger, and higher quality, than what exists in the literature.

Our models are primarily deployed internally for real workflows. As such, we maintain a tight feedback loop between usage, data, and model training.

**The role**

In this position, you will help train the next generation of chemistry models, and enable synthesis of previously inaccessible molecules.

Your work will span the full modeling stack. You will work with lab staff on data acquisition, train models of many different shapes and sizes, and deploy models directly into experimental workflows. You will build and help maintain infrastructure and abstractions for training a diverse set of models; this includes data pipelines and various system tasks such as parallelism strategies and quantization.

Ultimately, your role will be to train models with superhuman chemistry intuition and experimental capabilities.

**Education**

* No formal education is required. Ideal candidates will have some background in a deeply quantitative field, ideally with experience training ML models.

**Experience**

* Strong fundamentals in machine learning with a deep understanding of modern empirical/experimental ML
* Experience developing novel model training techniques or dealing with novel tasks or datasets
* Experience in a startup, research group, competition team, or other environment where you had significant ownership and limited resources is particularly relevant

**Skills**

* Familiarity with PyTorch or other machine learning frameworks
* Knowledge of basic machine learning theory
* Enthusiasm about working across the entire machine learning stack (data, training, inference, deployment)
* Comfort working across disciplines and learning unfamiliar technical areas as necessary
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Curiosity and excitement about chemistry
* A strong bias toward building, testing, and learning from real systems

**Potentially Relevant Experience**

Experience in any of the following areas would be useful, but we do not expect one person to have all of it:

* Training LLM models (particularly mid- and post-training)
* Machine learning systems (scaling, kernels, parallelism, etc.)
* Familiarity with chemistry models (retrosynthesis, mass spec modeling, etc.) or cheminformatics
* Active learning or other techniques suited for low-data regimes

**Additional requirements**

* Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary
* onepot works fully in person in our South San Francisco lab
* Ability to work safely in an active chemistry laboratory and around scientific equipment
* Note: This position does not involve lab work, but some projects may require an understanding of lab workflows
